Victory for the Ebenhaeser Land Claim

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
It’s rare to hear a successful land claim story but Ebenhaeser, a community of 2000 people on the lower Olifants River have been awarded their land back from which they were removed in 1926. It’s one of the biggest land restitution applications in the Western Cape and one of the longest unresolved claims but was finally successfully mediated under lockdown. The final restitution included substantial government funding to help the community manage the restored farms and, hopefully to avoid problems that have dogged other major land claims.

Summary:
But the process has been torturous and speaks to the local communities tenacity and Legal Aid lawyers to keep fighting despite the massive failures of the system sending the Ebenhaeser community from pillar to post. At one point the funding was supposed to come from the Land Claim Commission but the process was handed over to DAFF with out allocating the funds. While the farmers waited for funding they struggled to keep the farms going. They also inherited land with old very vines more than 25 years old and so the quality and yield was low, and after going through one of the worse droughts. The local wine Co-Op that had agreements in place to buy the grapes insisted they met their basic fixed costs despite the fact they had not received the capital to take over the farms and the vineyards were not as productive. How they had the patience and will to hang on is remarkable


Further information:
But after years of sheer determination they have turned the corner. Stella Organic Wines have signed a 20 year management agreement and will buy all the wines produced as well as provide mentoring and support to ensure the venture is a success. The Government funding has come in dribs and drabs and below what was agreed but they have a real partner and things are turning the corner. This last year the yield was up with a significant quantity more grapes harvested.
The farms that are run by the Communal Property Association as also getting equipment and mentoring from Stella Winery and are being supported to make the farms a success. So despite having all the odds staked against them Ebenhaeser community will finally farm their land and reap the benefits from this incredibly fertile area from which they were removed nearly 100 years ago
Stella Organic Winery has also entered into partnership with the mega farm and will buy all the grapes in a Fair Trade agreement and will mentor the farm and provide administrative and financial guidance.
Initially many of the farmers were unwilling to sell their land but have finally reached an agreement. Some of them will stay on their farms and lease them from the trust and others will hand them over at the end of the harvest.
The Ebenhaeser Communal Property Association (ECPA) will be entitled to take occupation of agricultural portions of those properties acquired “unconditionally” from the sellers, with all water rights, on 1st April 2021, and of houses, outbuildings, store rooms, sheds and other structures no later than 31 July 2021;
On this “unconditional” land, the sellers will be entitled to harvest grapes and other crops up to and including 1 April 2021;
“Conditional land” will be subject hand-over lease agreements between the ECPA and the individual sellers who will stay on the farms for stipulated period


Extra Budget Items:
Ebenezer is 4 hours drive from Cape Town and Derek has to catch a flight from JHB, he is the only presenter available to make the deadline. He will need a full travel day because flight are now 4 hours with the 2 hour pre book in times for Covid- So he will need full travel days either side of the two-day shoot. WE also need to interview the Lands Claim Commissioner in Cape Town and I have asked for that to be on Sat before Derek gets on the flight. I will also need a vehicle that can do dirt and farm roads, either hire one or use my car and pay the AA rates. WE will need 3 days per diem to cover the travel day

Script:


Script: Madelein Van Niekerk was a child in Grade 8, when she first started hearing talk about a land claim
Madelein “I didn’t understand, for me it was what do our people know about farming?
Script: Little did she know, it would become her life’s work. In August 2020, the people of Ebenhaeser won their 25 year battle. It’s small community, of about 2000 people, on the Cape West Coast, and they have fought the largest and longest land restitution claim, in the Western Cape
Madelein “ Personally, I didn’t think we would get it right. If you think back to where it all started, it was a very huge feeling. Actually I was too tired at that point to realise what we had achieved.
Link -There have been few success stories with land restitution claims in the last 25 years. But what stands out with this one is that the state not only returned people to their land, but gave them the funding and support to make a go of it
Script: The claim was R362-million rand, 196 million rand, was spent buying 44 properties, mostly under vineyards along the Olifants river, and the rest was for development funding. But 22 of the farmers in the earmarked area were unwilling to sell, holding out until 2020
Link: It’s been a long hard bitter struggle with both sides feeling aggrieved. We asked some of the farmers who land has been reclaimed for their side of the story but they weren’t interested in speaking to us
Script: David Mayson, a rural land reform and development consultant, started working with this claim, 15 years ago.
David: We initially thought that they were unwilling and I think in the 2015 2016 period, that might have been the case. But at that and as time went on, it became clear that I think they were wanting market related prices. In fact, I think they got a hell of a good deal because of the drought, the value of farms as it has decreased
Script: But this community's land struggle, dates back to 1831, when their leader, invited the German Rhenish Missionary Society, into the area
Link “Little did he know that his descendants would pay the price for his generosity and spend nearly 100 years trying to regain access to this fertile land.
Script: Ebenhaeser people were removed by the state segregationist policies, putting poor white farmers, on the fertile land. Nicolaas Le Roux, farms the land his father was removed to, in 1926
Derek “Did your father talk about the move here in 1926
Nicolaas ” It was an emotional day for them all when they had to leave, because they knew they were coming here to nothing.
Derek “ Your father Piet he grew up around Bloukraans which was a more fertile area
Nicolaas “ Pa said that the ground was very fertile with plenty of water. But when they were moved and came here, it was like they were in the veld. Everything they needed they had to do by hand because they had nothing, there were no tractors, there was nothing, they just had donkeys
Script: They had to dig sand canals to get water to their plots, and were given with no help from the government. They are still struggling to get a decent harvest out of the land, some have just abandoned their plots. The unemployment and poverty are desperate
Madelaine “The biggest stumbling block is the community, the unemployment, the drunkenness, the drug abuse and the dropout rate of our children. We have to get them back in a direction not so
Script: This restitution claim was awarded to the community, as opposed to individuals. Madeleine is the chair of the Ebenhaeser Communal Property Association, the legal entity, that is the custodian of the land. The reclaimed farms will be worked as one large unit, or mega farm, by Ebenhaeser Agri. Any profits from the megafarm, will go into the Ebenhaeser Development Trust.
Derek “So how many beneficiaries are there now
Madelaine “1714 members of the CPA
Derek Are they all happy with the arrangements
Madeleine “At the moment if I am honest, because of the long process, people aren’t so happy. People don’t understand what a complicated process it is, and people have become impatient.
David a lot of the reason for the delay, not only just in terms of the claim, but in terms of the other land reform components that affect Ebeneezer, it's got a lot to do with state capacity. On the one hand, the officials have got too much on their plate. Most of them don't understand anything about agriculture, and yet they pushing negotiations around the high value agriculture

Script: Only half of the farmers in the earmarked area were willing to sell up in 2015, and those were the worst properties with very old vineyards. The whole area was gripped in a devastating drought. To make matters worse, there was no money or support, because the promised development funding, was held up in the states bureaucratic processes

Mark At the time when we took over, we didn't have machinery. There was two farmers who actually helped us to make the first harvest possible.

Script: Mark Mennel was a trustee member at the time, and had returned home to Ebenheser, from a well paid job
Derek: the last few years must have been a struggle for you, Marc,

Mark: you can imagine you coming from a big salary and you earning nothing for 18 months. Some of the trustees at the time feel you shouldn't carry on because the government didn't give the money but my thinking was if we didn't do anything, they wouldn’t have faith in us

Derek: it was a tough battle.

Mark: It was a tough battle. We are not under the water anymore , my mouth is on top of the water. But I'm not fully out of the water yet.

Script: What’s turned this land claim around, was when Stellar Wines came on board in 2017, South Africa’s largest producer of organic and fair trade wines. CEO Willem Roussow, says corporates need to join hands with emerging farmers, and give them the support they deserve

Willem: The government are not able to make this a success if business and the local people that didn't work together and I think that's what we doing

Script: Ebenhaeser Agri now sells its grapes to Stellar, which pays a fair price. They converted to organic farming, and signed a 20 year management contract, which involves mentorship, training and sharing equipment. A Stellar farm manager, works alongside Mark

Willem “The first year we managed to get two point three million rand of produce to the winery and this year was four point six million. We will be able to plant new vines, but we planted in a high density manner so we can have the quality and the production at the same time.

Script: They also committed to only employing people from the Ebenheser. Robert Booysen, was a seasonal worker for 15 years, but is now employed full time, by Ebenhaeser Agri

Derek “Has your life really changed since you started working for Eben Agri
Robert “Big changes, at the moment I am happy about what I earn and how they treat us. It wasn't like it is now . They have made our houses a bit bigger, because we always just had two little rooms. They also pay for our electricity and water.
Script: In the final settlement in 2020, 87% of the land was bought, and those farms will be handed over after the harvest in April. The remaining incumbent farmers, have a rental agreement for the next 8 years. The State added an additional R9 million, to the CPA beneficiaries as compensation for benefits lost, due to the slow process. R24 million,was awarded to those descendants that had already left the area. But not everyone in the community is happy.
Nicolaas “Some of the members who maybe don’t have children feel they don't have descendants, so they want to receive the money so he or she can enjoy it. But then there are others who have children who feel we don’t want money, we want the land.
Derek “Surely Madeleine it was a nightmare dealing with some of these would be beneficiaries
Madeleine “Yes, we thought, or we as the committee thought, on the 12th June that we had finished all the negotiating, the journey was over. But that was when the journey began. We had to get the list right. The people who benefited must be 18 and older, and you must be living in Ebenhaeser
Derek” I am a beneficiary, how is my life going to change in the next 10 years
Madeline “The vision is that the project must grow. Money is not going to change people's lives immediately. But we must ensure that projects are established, so that there is an income every week in people’s households.
David: What's exciting about it is that on the one hand, you have a community owned company that is doing high value commercial farming… At the same time, you have small scale farmers on Ebeneezer. How does this commercial company assist and support these small scale farmers? … And the partnership with Stella winery, which is absolutely fundamental to that success.
Script: The state has built a new dam and pipeline to supply water to the plots, and Stellar have involved Woolworths and Distel to buy the produce
Madeline “ We are doing business with big companies. I ask the Lord to spare me for just another two years, so that I can just see how big the project gets, because the opportunities are there.
Script; The best farms will come in April, doubling the volume of grapes, and Ebenhaeser Agi, will become truly profitable
Willem Hopefully in the next three years we will have between 15 and 25 million rand that can go to the community

Robert For my family I will say that the future is bright. There are many opportunities, I must use every opportunity that I get and then I can be a better person in the future


Tues Promo 10 54 48 22 The Ebenhaeser land claim was finally settled under lockdown, it’s been a battle of biblical proportions. But the signs of hope are here to turn this bitter history around
Promo 11 “ Land Claims are bitter struggles but finally a 25 year battle the people of Ebenhaeser in the Western Cape not only got their fertile land back, but funding to make it a success.

Promo 11 “The people of Ebenheser in the Western Cape perseverance to keep fighting for their fertile land along the Olifants river was finally rewarded, and big business is helping they make a go of it

Promo 11: Ebenheser’s people in the Western Cape have got their fertile land back after an epic struggle. With support from the state and big corporates their mega farm will turn this bitter history around.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: It’s rare to hear a successful land claim story but Ebenhaeser, a community of 2000 people on the lower Olifants River have been awarded their land back from which they were removed in 1926. It’s one of the biggest land restitution applications in the Western Cape and one of the longest unresolved claims but was finally successfully mediated under lockdown. The final restitution included substantial government funding to help the community manage the restored farms and, hopefully to avoid problems that have dogged other major land claims.
metadata.Summary: But the process has been torturous and speaks to the local communities tenacity and Legal Aid lawyers to keep fighting despite the massive failures of the system sending the Ebenhaeser community from pillar to post. At one point the funding was supposed to come from the Land Claim Commission but the process was handed over to DAFF with out allocating the funds. While the farmers waited for funding they struggled to keep the farms going. They also inherited land with old very vines more than 25 years old and so the quality and yield was low, and after going through one of the worse droughts. The local wine Co-Op that had agreements in place to buy the grapes insisted they met their basic fixed costs despite the fact they had not received the capital to take over the farms and the vineyards were not as productive. How they had the patience and will to hang on is remarkable
metadata.Further information: But after years of sheer determination they have turned the corner. Stella Organic Wines have signed a 20 year management agreement and will buy all the wines produced as well as provide mentoring and support to ensure the venture is a success. The Government funding has come in dribs and drabs and below what was agreed but they have a real partner and things are turning the corner. This last year the yield was up with a significant quantity more grapes harvested. The farms that are run by the Communal Property Association as also getting equipment and mentoring from Stella Winery and are being supported to make the farms a success. So despite having all the odds staked against them Ebenhaeser community will finally farm their land and reap the benefits from this incredibly fertile area from which they were removed nearly 100 years ago Stella Organic Winery has also entered into partnership with the mega farm and will buy all the grapes in a Fair Trade agreement and will mentor the farm and provide administrative and financial guidance. Initially many of the farmers were unwilling to sell their land but have finally reached an agreement. Some of them will stay on their farms and lease them from the trust and others will hand them over at the end of the harvest. The Ebenhaeser Communal Property Association (ECPA) will be entitled to take occupation of agricultural portions of those properties acquired “unconditionally” from the sellers, with all water rights, on 1st April 2021, and of houses, outbuildings, store rooms, sheds and other structures no later than 31 July 2021; On this “unconditional” land, the sellers will be entitled to harvest grapes and other crops up to and including 1 April 2021; “Conditional land” will be subject hand-over lease agreements between the ECPA and the individual sellers who will stay on the farms for stipulated period
